bp: BaiJia serves a simple human wish: to make historical knowledge feel like a conversation instead of a distant archive. A reader may want to ask a poet about a poem, a general about a campaign, or a court official about family and political ties. Ordinary language models can imitate a historical voice, but they often rely on broad, uneven memory. Chinese historical figures create a sharper problem because the useful evidence is scattered across biographies, literary records, family relations, and descriptions of events, and the abstract calls this a low-resource historical setting. BaiJia tries to turn that scattered record into an open role-playing platform with 19,281 Chinese historical-character agents. The real object being built is not only a chatbot. It is a structured bridge between fragmented cultural records and interactive dialogue, so users can explore China's historical heritage through characters whose answers are shaped by documented lives rather than by vague historical style.
wh: The difficulty begins before any model is trained. A historical person is not described in one tidy file. One source may describe birth, death, office, or achievements. Another may contain poems or essays. Another may mention relatives. Another may place the person inside wars, dynastic events, or social circles. These pieces have different forms, levels of detail, and reliability. A role-playing agent must combine them because a believable answer depends on several kinds of evidence at once: what the person did, whom they knew, what they wrote, what events surrounded them, and what period they belonged to. A generic large language model may know famous names, but it will be weaker for less represented characters and may fill gaps with fluent invention. The hard tension is therefore completeness versus faithfulness. The platform must make characters engaging enough for dialogue while keeping them tied to fragmented historical data that may be sparse, uneven, or difficult to align.
naive: A smart beginner might collect a few paragraphs about each figure, paste them into a prompt, and ask a language model to answer in that person's voice. That can work for a famous character with clear records, but it breaks as soon as the question crosses sources. The model may know a biography but miss a family relation, know an event but not the person's role in it, or imitate an old-fashioned tone while saying something unsupported. Another beginner might train on raw historical text in bulk. That also fails because raw text does not tell the system which facts belong to which character or how biography, literature, relations, and events should constrain one answer.
ap: The core idea is to treat historical role-play as a grounding problem: before a model speaks as a character, the platform must gather and organize the evidence that defines that character. BaiJia compiles information for 19,281 Chinese historical figures and integrates multiple kinds of records, including biographical details, literary material, family relations, and historical events. This matters because role-playing is not just producing a lively sentence. The agent needs a stable identity and a boundary around what the character could plausibly know or say. By building a large open platform rather than a small set of manually curated examples, the paper aims to cover many figures, including those whose data is low-resource. The abstract does not specify every internal module, so the safe inference is mechanical rather than architectural: BaiJia improves foundational language models by supplying better character-specific historical context and evaluation targets for role-playing behavior.
mech: The mechanism starts with fragmented historical textual records in different forms. The platform has to turn those pieces into usable character material. First, records are gathered around a character: life facts, writings, kinship links, and events. Second, these pieces are integrated so they point to one historical identity instead of remaining separate fragments. In plain terms, the system has to decide that a family relation, a literary work, and an event mention all belong to the same person, or at least should be available when that person's agent answers. Third, the integrated material becomes the grounding information for a role-playing agent. When a user interacts with the platform, the chosen character agent can answer with reference to that character's documented life rather than relying only on the general memory of a base model. Fourth, the platform is evaluated against diverse foundational language models using six metrics. The abstract reports an average 10.2 percent improvement, which suggests that the BaiJia-specific construction changes measurable role-playing quality. The output of the whole process is an open website, codebase, and demonstration where users can converse with many historical-character agents. What is transformed is scattered historical text; what comes out is an organized set of character-specific dialogue agents.
math: The mathematics underneath is mostly about representation, matching, and evaluation, even though the abstract does not present equations. Representation means choosing what information about a person must be kept so a model can act consistently: biography, writings, family links, and events become a compact description of identity. Matching means connecting fragments that belong together. If records are scattered, the platform must align names, relations, works, and events so the right evidence is attached to the right character. This is the same everyday operation as sorting loose index cards into folders, except mistakes can make the agent attribute the wrong poem, relative, or event to a person. There is also a graph-like idea in family relations and events: people are nodes, relations or shared events are links, and links carry clues about what a character's world looked like. Evaluation adds measurement. Six metrics reduce role-playing quality into scores, allowing comparison against foundational models. The tradeoff is that scores make progress visible, but they may compress historical authenticity, conversational appeal, and factual grounding into numbers that cannot capture every human judgment. Probability-based learning is also implicit in the language model: from many examples, it estimates what words are likely to fit a character and context, but estimation can become false confidence when evidence is thin.
dots: BaiJia connects to the LLM agents theme because it treats a language model as a character-bearing agent, not just a text completer. It also connects to knowledge-graph and retrieval ideas in the conference. The abstract's list of biographies, literary works, family relations, and events is exactly the kind of material that benefits from organized links: people connected to relatives, texts, offices, and historical moments. Neighboring retrieval-augmented systems try to make models answer from the right outside evidence; BaiJia applies the same pressure to cultural history, where the evidence is fragmented and low-resource. It also sits near responsible generation and trust work, because the value of the platform depends on users receiving historically grounded interaction rather than entertaining invention. Compared with shopping, search, or workflow agents, this paper's surface task is heritage engagement, but the deeper problem is shared: an agent becomes useful only when its fluent language is tied to the right structured context.
ww: The approach should work better than a plain foundational model because it reduces the model's uncertainty about who it is supposed to be. A base model asked to role-play a historical character has to infer identity, period, relationships, style, and facts from whatever was absorbed during broad training. For well-known figures, that may be enough for a plausible answer. For many Chinese historical characters, especially in a low-resource historical setting, the model may have weak or uneven evidence. BaiJia changes the situation by assembling character-specific material before interaction. Biography anchors the person's life path. Literary records give examples of authored material or cultural role. Family relations place the person in a social network. Historical events place the person in time and circumstance. These constraints narrow the space of acceptable answers. The model is less free to drift into generic historical speech because the platform gives it concrete facts to preserve. The reported 10.2 percent average improvement across six metrics is consistent with this explanation: better organized grounding helps the agent become more character-specific, more faithful, and more useful for role-play than using diverse base models alone.
po: The payoff is an open large-scale role-playing platform for Chinese historical characters, with 19,281 agents rather than a small hand-built showcase. For users, the capability is interactive access to historical heritage: asking questions, exploring relationships, and encountering characters through dialogue. For researchers and builders, the contribution is a compiled low-resource historical resource that can be used with large language models for role-playing agents. The abstract reports comprehensive experiments and an average 10.2 percent improvement across six metrics compared with diverse foundational language models, so the claimed gain is not merely that the platform exists, but that its character-specific construction measurably improves role-playing behavior.
limits: Several assumptions must hold. The historical records gathered for each character must be accurate enough, correctly attached to the right person, and rich enough to guide dialogue. If a character has very sparse records, the agent may still invent details or speak with false confidence. The abstract does not state how conflicting sources are handled, how the six metrics judge historical faithfulness versus conversational style, or whether expert historians evaluated difficult cases. It also does not prove that a 10.2 percent average improvement is evenly distributed across famous and obscure figures. The platform's usefulness depends on data quality, source coverage, and safeguards against presenting plausible role-play as certain historical truth.
